_lid-_ "a company in the field" + _-madr_ "a man of a station" — a man of a following: the freed thrall still owing a former master, the drengr without a hall, the settled freeman of another people under Nordmal law; level 2 of the kinship kingdoms' ladder, which had no name of its own

_hring-_ "a ring given at a hall" + _-beri_ "one who bears a thing" — ring-bearer: the huscarl fed at the king's table, the clan leader's wife obeyed in his absence, the völva who takes the high seat, the honoured old at the door-seat; level 4, ungendered, chosen over the kept word _drengr_, which covers only one of the four doors

_hofs-_ "belonging to a hof" + _-madr_ "a man of a station" — the hof's acolyte: given to a hof young, taking its observances and its labour, years short of the priesthood; replaces Thraell, whose word is kept for the polity's rank 1, a man owned outright

_hrand-_ "a thing set down that will not be moved" (hard grade) + _-stead_ (normalising _-stad_, with Haukstad) — the settlement's own note calls it the kingdom's "principal stronghold and de facto capital," held by one dynasty for three generations; the retired _Bjorn-_ (bear) is not a name-stem, and the note's bear-lore is kept as the Bjorn-Königer dynasty's own, not the town's

_hörgs-_ (genitive of _hörgr_, "an open stone altar"), held from a sanctuary under the theophoric clause, + _-vangr_ "an open field" — the note describes a settlement "built around a sacred grove and standing stones," an open-air altar rather than ground held for itself, so it is held from a sanctuary and not from a stem

_hvalg-_ "a bay that shelters in any wind" (hard grade) + _-vík_ (unchanged) — the note gives only "Coastal Village"; a sheltering bay is the plainest sense a _-vík_ can carry for an otherwise undescribed coastal settlement

_hvarn-_ "water that will not freeze" (hard grade) + _-vík_ (unchanged) — the note gives only "Coastal Village"; chosen distinct from Brúnvík/Hvalgvík so the two undescribed coastal villages are not named from the same stock, and an inlet that stays open through winter is a fact worth a village's name

_nalth-_ "the last hour of a watch" (hard grade) + _-mark_ "a march, ground held at an edge" (unchanged) — the note gives only "Border Settlement"; a frontier holding is kept by its watch, and the retired _Frost-_ is not a name-stem

_thrald-_ "the pull of a current under calm water" (hard grade) + _-fjord_ (unchanged) — the note gives only "Fishing Village"; reading the fjord's current is a fisherfolk's essential skill, and the retired _Grey-_ names no stock at all

_dvarn-_ "a door that is never barred" (hard grade) + _-vík_ (unchanged) — the note gives only "Port Town"; an open harbor whose door is never barred to shipping is the plainest sense a port can carry

_krald-_ "a load a beast carries without complaint" (hard grade) + _-stead_ (normalising _-stad_, per the lexicon's own arithmetic) — the note gives only "Trading Post"; a trading post lives on the pack-trains that carry its goods in

_gnaldr-_ "floes grinding on one another" (hard grade) + _-fjord_ (unchanged) — the note describes "currents that pull wrongly and lights that dance beneath the ice in winter"; the grinding of pack ice is the fjord's own defining, eerie sound, kept distinct from Ravensholm/Ódholm's Odin-held name so the two raven-adjacent settlements are not named from the same source

_vrath-_ "the temper iron takes from the fire" (hard grade) + _-havn_ (unchanged) — the note calls this Norgaad's "Iron Harbor," a militant port of smithies and a standing garrison; the tempering fire is the closest name-stem sense to the retired Iron gloss

_knarv-_ "a joint made to take strain" (hard grade) + _-vík_ (unchanged) — the note gives only "Harbor Town"; chosen distinct from Járnhavn/Vrathavn (also retired an Iron- name) for the structural sense of a dock built to bear a harbor's strain, rather than the fire that tempers a blade

_hnarv-_ "the notch cut to count off a year" (hard grade) + _-dal_ (unchanged) — the note gives only "Valley Settlement"; a dale is itself a notch cut into the land, echoing the stem's own sense, and the retired _Kvenn-_ opens on "kv," which Nordmal does not open on

_marv-_ "the grain in worked antler" (hard grade) + _-stead_ (unchanged) — the note names it only "Town"; the stem is chosen for its plain, workaday craft sense rather than claiming a distinguishing feature the note does not state

held from a god under the theophoric clause: Ódinn's settled name _Ódvar_ (concordance, deity) clipped to its first element _ód-_, + _-holm_ (unchanged) — the note is explicit that the settlement grew up around Odin's own temple and "was founded in the age of heroes, when Odin himself walked the earth," the corpus's clearest case of a place held from a god rather than from the ground alone

_ralth-_ "how far a voice carries over water" (hard grade) + _-holm_ (normalising _-holme_, per the lexicon's own arithmetic) — the note names it only "Town"; hailing across open water is the natural sense for an otherwise undescribed holm

_gnarth-_ "the set of a jaw that will not open" (hard grade) + _-borg_ (unchanged) — the note gives only "Fortified Town"; the stem's unyielding sense matches a defended stronghold where no further detail is given
_flarn-_ "a flake of stone split off by frost" (hard grade) + _-brekka_ (unchanged) — the note gives only "Mountain Settlement"; frost-shattered scree is what a slope in the high country is made of

_tvarn-_ "two things that must be counted as one" (hard grade) + _-mark_ (unchanged) — the note is explicit that the town "rises... at the confluence of two swift rivers" on the kingdom's edge, which the stem names directly and the retired _Stein-_ (stone) does not

_knalth-_ "an oath that binds without being written" (hard grade) + _-stead_ (unchanged) — the note names it only "Fortified Town"; an unwritten binding oath matches a garrison town's shared defense where no further detail is given
_dvalg-_ "sleep taken standing, on watch" (hard grade) + _-heim_ (unchanged) — the note names it only "Settlement"; a watchful rest suits an ordinary home where no more specific detail is given
_brald-_ "a fire banked to keep overnight" (hard grade) + _-heim_ (unchanged) — the note names it only "Settlement"; a banked hearth-fire is the plainest sense a home can carry
_tvalg-_ "the lesser of a pair" (hard grade) + _-gard_ (unchanged) — the note names it only "Town"; the stem is chosen for its plainness, marking an ordinary holding rather than a distinguished one

_skrald-_ "a cry the wind carries further than it should" (hard grade) + _-borg_ (unchanged) — the note describes a "Hill Fort"; an exposed height where a warning carries unnaturally far on the wind answers the retired _Vind-_ (wind) sense while grounding it in a real name-stem

_vrild-_ (middle grade) + `-mýl` (a man) — son of Hrafnkell, so takes the grade after his father's hard; vrald 'the weight a rope will take' fits a young protector shouldering the burden of keeping others from the harm his own family suffered
_ralth-_ (hard grade) + `-thýra` (a woman) — a street-singer whose ballads move listeners in taverns and alleys; ralth 'how far a voice carries over water' is a singer's own gift
_hvalg-_ (hard grade) + `-vir` (a man) — an innkeeper whose tavern is 'a sanctuary' and 'a refuge'; hvalg 'a bay that shelters in any wind' is exactly that
_gnaldr-_ (hard grade) + `-thann` (a man) — a soldier ground down by decades of campaigns; gnaldr 'floes grinding on one another' is the friction and attrition of a life at war
_tvirn-_ (middle grade) + `-vir` (a man) — a clanless skald who 'plays both sides,' bending truth as needed; tvarn 'two things that must be counted as one' names a man who is never only one thing
_hlisk-_ (middle grade) + `-thann` (a man) — a thatcher of deep quiet who reads the weather before he reads a room; hlask 'the hush that follows heavy snow' is his own stillness
_vrath-_ (hard grade) + `-mýl` (a man) — a shipwright with a latent gift for fire; vrath 'the temper iron takes from the fire' is his own magic, literally

_thilm-_ (middle grade) + `-selda` (a woman) — an innkeeper whose stern exterior hides real warmth, and whose inn is 'a space of true sanctuary'; thalm 'the still air inside a drift' is the calm she keeps at the center of a hard world
_tvarn-_ (hard grade) + `-ynda` (a woman) — a seidr-woman who walks between the mortal and spirit worlds; tvarn 'two things that must be counted as one' names exactly that liminal standing
_thrald-_ (hard grade) + `-orv` (a man) — a mercenary whose stoic exterior 'covers a man surprisingly troubled'; thrald 'the pull of a current under calm water' is exactly that hidden undertow

_knalth-_ (hard grade) + `-rinna` (a woman) — a teamster whose word is proverbially binding ('if Gunnvör promised delivery, that delivery would manifest'); knalth 'an oath that binds without being written' is her whole reputation
_svulth-_ (deep grade) + `-thýra` (a woman) — a solitary trapper of the deep wilderness, cold and isolated by trade; svalth 'the cold that comes off open water' names her chosen isolation
_krald-_ (hard grade) + `-mýl` (a man) — a woodcutter who bears his solitary labor and his old grief without complaint; krald 'a load a beast carries without complaint' is his whole temperament
_flarn-_ (hard grade) + `-thýra` (a woman) — a potter so exacting she 'shatters finished pieces' that miss the mark; flarn 'a flake of stone split off by frost' is her own perfectionism made literal

_dvarn-_ (hard grade) + `-vir` (a man) — a tentmaker who believes 'good shelter saves lives'; dvarn 'a door that is never barred' is the whole philosophy of his craft. Brothers with Thjótharr, so both take the hard grade; Bjalfi is his son and takes the grade after

_dvilg-_ (middle grade) + `-thýra` (a woman) — an enslaved household servant who has 'perfected the art of appearing submissive while observing everything'; dvalg 'sleep taken standing, on watch' is exactly her forced, constant vigilance

_thrild-_ (middle grade) + `-vir` (a man) — a tailor whose 'passion held under disciplined control' hides beneath a quiet reserve; thrald 'the pull of a current under calm water' is that submerged intensity
_hrand-_ (hard grade) + `-rinna` (a woman) — a thatcher whose roofs and whose stubborn resolve both outlast the ordinary; hrand 'a thing set down that will not be moved' names her durability
_hnurv-_ (deep grade) + `-thýra` (a woman) — a dyer who has spent decades counting out her craft's slow mastery; hnarv 'the notch cut to count off a year' names that patient accumulation

_snurv-_ (deep grade) + `-thann` (a man) — a thatcher famed for forecasting weather with uncanny accuracy; snarv 'the hour before weather arrives' is his own gift, deep grade for his age and long widowhood

_tvurn-_ (deep grade) + `-thann` (a man) — a shaman torn between Nordmen tradition and southern academy, ergi and honored, belonging fully to neither; tvarn 'two things that must be counted as one' is the whole of his contradiction

_enth-_ (hard grade) + `-orv` (a man) — a court jester who lives on 'the far side' of every mask he wears, never quite reaching the person underneath; enth 'the far side of a pass' names that unreachable far shore
_hlirth-_ (middle grade) + `-selda` (a woman) — a shield-maiden who holds a warband's duty to defend her home ground; hlirth 'the slope a hall is set on' names the ground she stands for
_hvarn-_ (hard grade) + `-thann` (a man) — a sailor whose whole life is the sea; hvarn 'water that will not freeze' is literally his working element
_glirv-_ (middle grade) + `-rinna` (a woman) — a textile artist absorbed in color, form and light; glarv 'light lying flat on water' is the visual quality her patterned work seeks

_brald-_ (hard grade) + `-thann` (a man) — a tentmaker who guards his family's craft and keeps its standard burning against a faster, cheaper age; brald 'a fire banked to keep overnight' is that tended, unyielding continuity (ending chosen to avoid duplicating an already-named background character elsewhere in the corpus)

_thrask-_ (hard grade) + `-orv` (a man) — a former thrall of 'contained fury,' worn down by his condition like a keel scraping shingle; thrask names that grinding friction (ending chosen to avoid duplicating an already-named background character elsewhere in the corpus)

_skrald-_ (hard grade) + `-thann` (a man) — a clothier obsessed with recognition and 'immortality through his art'; skrald 'a cry the wind carries further than it should' names a reputation that wants to carry further than it has earned. Brother of Hrafnkell, hard grade to match
_ulth-_ (deep grade) + `-orv` (a man) — a man enslaved and burning for freedom above all else; ulth 'the limit a claim reaches' names the boundary of what is owed him and what he means to reclaim
_thulm-_ (deep grade) + `-vir` (a man) — a potter who guards patient tradition against fashionable haste; thulm 'the still air inside a drift' is his own unhurried stillness

_rulth-_ (deep grade) + `-vir` (a man) — a herder who has followed livestock across windswept highlands his whole life; rulth 'how far a voice carries over water' extends here to a herder's call across open ground
_thalm-_ (hard grade) + `-thann` (a man) — a glassworker of 'measured calm,' precise and unhurried; thalm 'the still air inside a drift' matches his temperament
_alth-_ (hard grade) + `-ynda` (a woman) — a chandler pushing her craft to where beauty and utility meet; alth 'the limit a claim reaches' names that outer edge she keeps testing

_knilth-_ (middle grade) + `-thann` (a man) — a saga-keeper of an oral tradition, sworn to hold his clan's history without ever writing it; knalth 'an oath that binds without being written' is the whole of his craft
_hlask-_ (hard grade) + `-orv` (a man) — a woodcutter of 'deep silence' who thinks before he speaks; hlask 'the hush that follows heavy snow' is that same stillness
_svalth-_ (hard grade) + `-rinna` (a woman) — raised on the storm-battered coast of Nordheim; svalth 'the cold that comes off open water' names the hard coast that shaped her

_tvalg-_ (hard grade) + `-thann` (a man) — a jester who is always, by profession, the lesser figure beside the noble he entertains, however much true influence he holds; tvalg 'the lesser of a pair' names that public standing
_vruld-_ (deep grade) + `-orv` (a man) — a guardsman who carries the weight of duty and searches for a cause worth it; vruld 'the weight a rope will take' names that load

_hlarth-_ (hard grade) + `-vir` (a man) — a giant of a woodsman bound to the forest itself; hlarth 'the slope a hall is set on' is the ground he has become part of. The note's own worked example of a lawful name
_gnuldr-_ (deep grade) + `-thýra` (a woman) — 'a fusion of different beings' abandoned by her creator; gnuldr 'floes grinding on one another' names her composite, ground-together nature
_skrild-_ (middle grade) + `-mýl` (a man) — a war-leader 'whose war cry was said to echo like thunder'; skrild 'a cry the wind carries further than it should' is that carrying voice
_svilth-_ (middle grade) + `-selda` (a woman) — eerily calm even walking through fire; svilth 'the cold that comes off open water' is an ironic, deliberate coolness set against her flame

_knalth-_ (hard grade) + `-thann` (a man) — wants to 'codify the scattered oral laws' into something written and binding; knalth 'an oath that binds without being written' is exactly the old order he means to put into writing
_vrith-_ (middle grade) + `-orv` (a man) — a warrior whose heart 'burned with the very fire of Súrtr'; vrith 'the temper iron takes from the fire' is that same tempering by flame
_glurv-_ (deep grade) + `-selda` (a woman) — a merchant devoted to Fréyja who sees value and prosperity in everything; glurv 'light lying flat on water' is that glint of worth she finds everywhere
_hlusk-_ (deep grade) + `-mýl` (a man) — a sorcerer of quiet, vile menace; hlusk 'the hush that follows heavy snow' turned to a colder, more sinister silence
_skulf-_ (deep grade) + `-mýl` (a man) — a provocateur whose words crack the social order the way ice cracks before it gives; skulf 'the shudder in ice before it gives' is that same fracture
_dvulg-_ (deep grade) + `-ynda` (a woman) — a thief who studies a target for weeks before striking; dvulg 'sleep taken standing, on watch' is a spy's patient, wakeful stillness
_hnirv-_ (middle grade) + `-mýl` (a man) — a seer and runemaster who keeps the accumulated lore of generations; hnirv 'the notch cut to count off a year' names that long tally of remembered years

_krild-_ (middle grade) + `-thann` (a man) — a warrior who would 'rather absorb a hundred blows than deliver one unjust strike'; krild 'a load a beast carries without complaint' is the burden of a shield-bearer
_vruth-_ (deep grade) + `-vir` (a man) — a blacksmith who reveres 'the raw power' of the forge; vruth 'the temper iron takes from the fire' is literally his trade
_mirv-_ (middle grade) + `-rinna` (a woman) — a farmer blessed by Fréyr whose gift is the grain itself; mirv 'the grain in worked antler' echoes the harvest that names her
_rilth-_ (middle grade) + `-orv` (a man) — a wandering skald whose voice carries the sagas from village to village; rilth 'how far a voice carries over water' is his craft itself
_hvirn-_ (middle grade) + `-orv` (a man) — a sorcerer of cold, remorseless calculation; hvirn 'water that will not freeze' names that unyielding, glacial calm

_tvilg-_ (middle grade) + `-orv` (a man) — a man merged with Dreadspawn essence, trapped between two natures at war; tvilg 'the lesser of a pair' names the half of him that keeps losing ground to the other
_hvulg-_ (deep grade) + `-selda` (a woman) — a sailor-warrior devoted to defending her people from the sea's dangers; hvulg 'a bay that shelters in any wind' is the protection she offers others
_dvirn-_ (middle grade) + `-mýl` (a man) — a trickster guided by Lôki who slips past any barrier; dvirn 'a door that is never barred' fits a man no lock or persona keeps out

_vrald-_ (hard grade) + `-orv` (a man) — a warrior who carries the weight of justice with one hand, as Týr carries the weight of his own sacrifice; vrald 'the weight a rope will take' is that burden (ending chosen to avoid duplicating an already-named background character elsewhere in the corpus)
_murv-_ (deep grade) + `-selda` (a woman) — blessed by Fréyja with a voice and charm polished by long practice at court; murv 'the grain in worked antler' names that fine, worked quality
_hvilg-_ (middle grade) + `-thýra` (a woman) — a shieldmaiden who balances the blade with Ódinn's deeper teachings; hvilg 'a bay that shelters in any wind' extends a shield's own sense to a person
_brild-_ (middle grade) + `-selda` (a woman) — a healer whose touch 'brings warmth and life'; brild 'a fire banked to keep overnight' is the tended warmth she brings to the wounded
_skalf-_ (hard grade) + `-orv` (a man) — a warrior whose 'hammer blows echo like thunder'; skalf 'the shudder in ice before it gives' is that same shattering crack
_knirv-_ (middle grade) + `-thýra` (a woman) — a woman who transformed suffering under great pressure into lasting power; knirv 'a joint made to take strain' is exactly that
